texto: **Brauchen** (need) + **zu** + infinitive means «need to do something»: **Du brauchst nicht zu kommen** (no need to come). With **nicht** he states that something is not necessary, not that it is prohibited. It's a standard and regular construction.
You can also carry **kein**: **Du brauchst kein Brot zu kaufen** (you don't need to buy bread).

With **müssen** it is an obligation: **Du musst kommen** (you have to come). With **brauchen … nicht zu** it is not necessary: **Du brauchst nicht zu kommen** (you do not need to come). Eye with the false friend: **brauchen** does not mean «use», means «need».

filas: Du brauchst kein Brot zu kaufen.
You don't need to buy bread.

frases.de: Mein Gerät ist kaputt. Muss ich es zurückbringen?
frases.es: Mi aparato está roto. ¿Tengo que devolverlo?
frases.en: My device is broken. Do I have to give it back?

frases.de: Nein, du brauchst es nicht zurückzubringen. Der Kundendienst kommt zu dir.
frases.es: No, no hace falta que lo devuelvas. El servicio de atención al cliente viene a tu casa.
frases.en: No, you don't have to give it back. The customer service comes to your house.

frases.de: Super, dann brauche ich kein Paket zu schicken.
frases.es: Genial, entonces no necesito enviar ningún paquete.
frases.en: Great, so I don't need to send any packages.
analisis: brauche ich kein Paket zu schicken
I don't need to send any packages.

frases.de: Genau. Die Rechnung brauchst du nicht zu drucken.
frases.es: Exacto. No hace falta que imprimas la factura.
frases.en: Exactly. You don't have to print the bill.

bloques.pregunta: What does «du brauchst nicht zu kommen» mean?

opciones.explicacion: That would be «müssen» denied, with obligation.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «You have to come.» (obligation)?

bloques.frase: Du brauchst kein Brot zu kaufen.

opciones.texto: You don't need to buy bread.

bloques.pregunta: What does this job indication mean?
bloques.frase: Du brauchst heute nicht ins Büro zu kommen.

opciones.texto: You don't have to come to the office today.
opciones.explicacion: «brauchen ... nicht zu» expresses no need (optional / not mandatory).

opciones.texto: You have a strict obligation to come to the office today.
Access to the office building is totally prohibited.
opciones.explicacion: That would require a ban with «dürfen» denied («Du darfst nicht kommen»).

bloques.pregunta: What form of «bestellen» is used as a participle for «has been ordered»?

bloques.frase: Du brauchst die Rechnung heute nicht zu ___ .

opciones.explicacion: With the construction «brauchen ... nicht zu» the lexic verb is placed in infinitive at the end.
It is participle II, incompatible with the «zu» particle.
It's the conjugated form of second person, not a terminal infinitive.

intro: Today we learn to say «I don't have to.». «brauchen» and «zu» express the lack of need, the opposite of «müssen».
